instructions: Asha introduction (the memory of bear wounds inside walls no bear could climb): the chapter never says Asha was Devan's sister, so ch 16's "his sister's blood" is the first time a reader learns it. In the first sentence that names Asha, state that she was his sister and also his second at the fort. Use one clause and a concrete marker, such as 'Asha, his sister, his second on this wall', so the rage that pulls him to the ledge is personal from the start. Owner's note overrides the outline's 'his second' alone.

Keep without change: the turning written as 'the most private thing he had ever seen. He did not look away. That was the job, and it was also the crime.' Also keep the palm on the third slat 'as he would on a horse's neck', the 'Rice and plantains... I'm hungry' lie to Janu, and the shut-eyes beat at the dawn return. These are the owner's marked strengths. Do not trim them to make room for the sister clause.

Consistency check for the sister fact added in ch 2: in the private-face memory of Asha learning every recruit's name, make sure the wording doesn't contradict her being his sister. 'His sister had done that' or 'Asha had done that' both work. Do not call her only 'his second' in a way that implies no blood tie. Change nothing else.

Asha's chest scene, where Devan tells Neela about Asha: the outline lists her as 'his second at the fort'. Per the owner, she is both his sister and his second. Have Devan say both to Neela, for example 'My sister. My second, after.' This is the first time Neela hears it, so ch 16's 'his sister's blood' and ch 30 hold for her as well as the reader. Keep 'I won't answer that' to 'How?' unchanged.

Neela's reread, from 'The shutters had gone up barred...' through 'She had never once asked who told Janu': it walks clues C01 to C05 in order like an evidence log. That is the main reason the chapter scored 3.5. Cut the section to about half its current length.

Within the cut reread, make one or two items land physically, in the present. For example, she crosses to the west window and lifts the bar he no longer needs, feeling its weight in her hands. Or she stands still and hears the kennels quiet below, no hound baying at the scent of her. Let her realise through the object or the sound, not through a list.

After the physical beat, let the rest arrive as one quick cascade: short clauses, the unlit lamp, 'the cat', Janu's stories cut off, the rice. Each gets a few words, with no attribution of who called what. Delete recap lines such as 'Bhaskaran's lads called it privacy, Gopan called it Janu's old tale, Janu called it the damp, and Chinna ran a wager on it' entirely.
Keep the Chathu-and-the-sweets paragraph at full length. It is the part of the reread that does discovery rather than recap.
Keep the withdrawal speech unchanged: 'I can't unwitness myself. I can only tell you I won't, and let you watch whether I do.'

Keep the ending unchanged: the breath-hitch realisation ('The hitch had never been sleep. It had been him, all twenty nights, and now he was giving it to her on purpose, so she could count him.'). Also keep her refusal to trust ('The first mistake ended her. The other only hurt').

Year count: wherever the chapter says 'twenty-one of my twenty-seven years', make it plain that this counts from her guild intake at six, not from her first resin. One clause is enough, such as 'twenty-one of my twenty-seven years on the guild's page'. This keeps it consistent with ch 31's resin burning her 'for eleven years' since she was sixteen. The book's figure for guild years is twenty-one. Use it everywhere.

Check that 'his sister's blood' still reads naturally now that ch 2 and ch 12 establish Asha as his sister. No change is needed unless the line explains the relationship as if it were new. If it does, trim that explanation.

Consistency check for ch 30's 'crown writ' line. The summary says the pass was sealed 'with Neela's name as witness'. If ch 29 shows Neela signing the sealing writ as witness, make that one beat clear on the page. She signs her name, as his wife, to a border-law sealing under the padippura roof. Add one line of her interiority that marks it as a change from her ch 23 refusal: this is a border writ in her married name, not an odiyan's testimony before the queen. If ch 29 does not show her signing anything, add nothing here and follow the 'otherwise cut' branch in ch 30.

The re-explanation passage that relists the shutters, hounds, sentry and Janu's stories ('The second dusk I barred them. The hounds went to the kennel that same night...'): the reader solved all of this at the ch 16 midpoint. Cut the list. Keep only what is new. He decided never to use what he'd seen before he picked up the bar on the second dusk. And he says why, in his own exact register: the reason he chose, not the inventory of what he did. Two to four lines of dialogue at most.

Spend the words saved from that cut on the trust moment at the base of his skull, the real payoff. Have him describe her fingers on the killing point and the three counted breaths in concrete, physical terms: what he felt under her fingertips, what he counted while she counted, the moment her hand lifted. Let Neela answer or react so the beat is an exchange, not a speech. Keep his interiority short and turned into a choice. No paragraph over 220 words.

Ownership language: replace 'I wanted the thing to stay mine to hold, and no one else's' with a line in his usual exactness that doesn't claim possession of her or her secret. Model it on ch 31's 'It's yours. I'm only holding it.' One option: 'I wanted to be the only one who carried it, so no one else could set it down on you.' His arc is 'I don't want to own anyone', so no word in his mouth should frame her or her turning as his.

'You've just watched me sign a crown writ': unclear, because in ch 23 she refused to testify before the crown. If ch 29 has her sign the sealing writ as witness, state it here in one clause and own it as a change. For example: 'You watched me put my name to the sealing writ, beside yours. Ten days ago I wouldn't have.' Otherwise cut the line.

'Neela is the name I have for you' reads as half-formed. She has no known birth name, and the book will pursue that as a series thread. Either make it concrete and exact ('Neela is the only name you've given me. It's the one I'll use until you give me another') or cut it.

'I wrote it with your name beside mine' reads as half-formed. Tie it to a specific document. If ch 29's sealing writ carries her signature, say so plainly ('On the sealing writ I wrote your name beside mine'). If no such document exists in ch 29, cut the line.

'You've bled on me before I've had my supper' reads as half-formed. Either cut it, or make it a concrete reaction to the tooth drawing blood on both their thumbs, phrased so it can't be misread. Keep the tooth-drawing-blood-on-both-thumbs beat itself unannounced. The owner likes that it shows the wound-share without explaining.
Year count: change any 'twenty years' in dialogue to 'twenty-one years' to match ch 16 and ch 31's vow.
Keep the callbacks unchanged: 'I'm not counting the door.' / 'Six.' and 'Say it again, so I can check.' / 'It holds.'

The Ittan interruption: 'A man who offers at night can take it back by noon' and 'He had waited all that time to be caught' don't parse. Rewrite so the cost is plain. Ittan sends word he will talk now. A man like Ittan may change his mind by morning, so the first offer is now or never. Neela knows this and chooses the dawn hour with Devan anyway. Give her one short line of interiority or dialogue naming that trade: she is spending Ittan's confession to keep the hour. Cut 'He had waited all that time to be caught' unless it can be made to state a clear fact in one plain clause.

Vow title-drop: 'My promises have teeth in them. I'll keep them with those' is the line a reviewer would quote as cheesy. Cut it from the public vow. The naming of Raiu, Ammu and every living soul in the house already carries the vow. If you keep a version, move it out of the vow into a private aside. Devan answers it dryly and exactly, so it reads as a joke between them, not a declaration to the courtyard.

Packet logistics, set-up for ch 32: keep Muthu carrying the grey packet into the guardroom. Add one line at that point that sets up the routine handover in ch 32. For example, Muthu says he'll leave it with the warden for the spring rider, the way the household's post always waits out the closed pass. Do not show anyone opening it.

Year count: change 'twenty years' in dialogue to 'twenty-one years' to match ch 16 and the vow's 'twenty-one of my twenty-seven years'. Keep 'burned her for eleven years' and 'since I was sixteen' as they are; they are consistent.

Keep unchanged: Muthu's 'I'll write the weather' and Neela's 'Then write my name spelled right'; the leopard's head pushed into his hand after 'Not the cat. Neela.'; the pebble set on the sill. Keep the dawn return with her leading the explicit scene. It changes the relationship because she lets him see the return for the first time. Keep his 'It's yours. I'm only holding it' as written. It is the model for the ownership fixes in ch 30 and ch 32.

'You were never a line. You were the wife I kept.' is a stock comfort line, and 'the wife I kept' contradicts his arc in a book about leashes. Replace it with his exactness and no possessive framing. For example: 'You were never a line. You were the one thing on that list I didn't have to guess at.' Or, closer to ch 31's model: 'You were never a line. You were the person I was holding it for.'

Neela's reply 'Don't be kind. I can't think when you're kind' is also stock. Replace it with a reply in her own register, which counts and checks. For example, she asks him to say it again so she can check, or she answers with a precise question that shows she is testing the words and finds they hold. Don't reuse ch 30's exact 'It holds' exchange; vary it so it isn't a repeated image within three chapters.

Packet logistics: Muthu would know his packet left the guardroom, so 'had taken the grey packet out of the guardroom himself' plus wanting Muthu 'to go on believing he was not' read doesn't hold. Replace it with an open, routine custody handover in Muthu's sight. Devan takes the packet 'for the spring rider' and locks it in the strongbox with the rest of the post, and Muthu shrugs it off as ordinary. Keep it unopened. This closes the gap and keeps Muthu feeling unread, which the hinge depends on.
After the custody line, Devan still sends Muthu to the Resin House. Make sure nothing in that order suggests Devan has read the packet. Muthu should leave believing his letters are untouched.

The grille scene with Ittan: make it read as the price of Neela's ch 31 choice. Ittan, offered the dawn hour and refused it, has now closed up and gives them only 'You've no idea whose hand I am' or silence. Let Devan or Neela register in one beat that the offer is gone.

Keep unchanged: the queen's green sunbird seal set beside the cut wedding-gift wax; Ittan's letter about his wife's willow bark, which keeps him from being a strawman; the evidence hidden behind the creaking third slat; the book-two question; and the ending 'Then I'll come.'
